- Success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 350ms for 1k qps simulated load; embedding similarity recall >= 92% on the canonical eval set; cost target <= $0.002/token.
- Constraints: production data cannot leave Acme network for compliance team review (likely need VPC option), but initial evaluation can use hosted sandbox for speed.

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline:
1) Week 0 (this week): confirm environment choice and ownership.
2) Week 1: provisioning + run simple smoke tests (latency, correctness).
3) Week 2-3: full load tests, embedding/QA evals, regression checks.
4) Week 4: debrief and decision meeting — go/no-go.

Ownership
- Redwood: provisioning, perf testing harness, runbook for access. (Rafael on SRE/SE)
- Acme: provide eval dataset, technical contact for VPC networking, sign SOW for dedicated sandbox if needed. (Alice/Bob)

- Share eval dataset link (or a small sample) and the contact for security/compliance questions.

Next steps

Hi Alice / Bob — quick technical note on environment tradeoffs and what we recommend for your goals.

Short answer: start hosted sandbox for speed, but plan a parallel VPC trial if compliance requires it. If you need production-like latency fidelity, the dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool) best approximates Dedicated behavior.

Options explained:
- Hosted sandbox (fastest): pre-provisioned shared capacity in our hosted environment. Pros: fastest to spin up (~4 hours), no infra work from Acme, integrated telemetry. Cons: shared hardware can show lower tail latency variability vs dedicated hardware; data persists only per our retention policy (we can enable stricter retention on request).

- Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity): reserved GPU pool on Redwood Dedicated but isolated in a customer sandbox. Pros: identical serving runtime/kernels as Redwood Dedicated, predictable throughput & tail latency. Cons: longer lead time to provision (1-3 business days) and cost overhead.

- VPC trial (network-isolated): private deployment into your VPC with optional on-prem adapter. Pros: meets strict compliance; data never leaves your network. Cons: longest provisioning time (typically 3-7 business days), requires networking/trust setup, and we’ll need a small checklist from your infra team.

What we need for VPC provisioning (if you choose that path):
- VPC ID, subnets to use, and preferred availability-zone(s)
- A bastion or jump-host plan for our SEs (or VPN/peering details)
- Egress policy and any IP allowlists for telemetry callbacks
- KMS key ARN if you want us to use your key for data encryption at rest

Attached is a short runbook that outlines the smoke tests we’ll run and the data we collect during week 1.

[Attachment: poc-runbook.pdf (PDF) — 1.2MB stub]

If you want, we can spin up a hosted sandbox today and run a baseline latency/cost report; Rafael can drive the smoke tests and share results within 24 hours.

Thanks,
